title: How a Delta Grows

endcard.line: Pictures: NASA, Landsat 7 and Space Shuttle Columbia crew (public domain)

segments.say: Seen from space, the mouths of the Ganga and the Brahmaputra look like the branches of a tree. This is the largest delta on Earth.

anim.title: How a delta grows
items: The river slows at the sea
It drops its silt and sand

segments.say: A river carries silt. When it reaches the sea, it slows down and drops that load. The silt piles up, blocks the way, and the river splits into smaller channels, called distributaries.

anim.title: Why 'delta'?
items: Shaped like the Greek letter Δ
Coarse sand drops first, fine clay last
New land grows out into the sea

segments.say: Over centuries the land grows outward in a fan, shaped like the Greek letter delta. That's where the name comes from.

left.title: Delta
items: Flow east to the Bay of Bengal

right.title: Estuary
items: Flow west to the Arabian Sea

segments.say: Most big rivers of peninsular India flow east and build deltas. But the Narmada and the Tapi flow west, through rift valleys, and end in estuaries instead.
They carry less silt, they run through hard rock, and the tides wash out what they bring.
For GS One: a river slows, drops its silt, and splits. East-flowing rivers build deltas; the Narmada and the Tapi make estuaries.

sources: NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography, ch. 7 (Landforms and their Evolution): deltas form where rivers deposit their load at the mouth; coarser material settles first; distributaries

NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 3 (Drainage System): Ganga–Brahmaputra delta is the world's largest; Narmada and Tapi flow west through rift valleys and form estuaries; east-flowing peninsular rivers form deltas
UNESCO World Heritage List, The Sundarbans (Bangladesh) and Sundarbans National Park (India): largest mangrove forest in the world

quiz.q: Why does a river drop its silt at the sea?
options: The sea pushes it back up
quiz.why: A slower river can't carry its load, so the silt settles.

options: Smaller channels a river splits into near its mouth
Rivers that join the main river
quiz.why: The silt blocks the way and the river splits into distributaries.

quiz.q: Which river ends in an estuary, not a delta?
quiz.why: The Narmada and the Tapi flow west and form estuaries.
